tsmc_exposure.question: Which funds are most exposed to a TSMC manufacturing disruption?
tsmc_exposure.answer: Both funds are materially exposed to a disruption at Taiwan Semiconductor (TSMC). Four held issuers — NVIDIA, AMD, Apple and Broadcom — each disclose a critical foundry dependence on TSMC, so the exposure aggregates across positions rather than sitting in a single name. In the Demo Focused Growth Fund those four names total 37.5% of assets; in the Demo Growth Fund they total 27.5%. The dependence is also second-order: TSMC's own leading-edge output depends critically on EUV lithography from ASML, so a single ASML/EUV shock would propagate to every one of those holdings.

citations.title: TSMC FY2024 20-F
citations.span: Our leading-edge manufacturing depends on extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography systems supplied by ASML

graph_paths.label: Demo Focused Growth Fund → NVIDIA → TSMC

plan.strategy: graph-first multi-hop traversal, then ground each edge in a cited span
steps: Traverse inbound SUPPLIES_TO (criticality=critical) to find dependent issuers
Traverse inbound HOLDS to attribute each issuer to funds and sum weights
Traverse outbound SUPPLIES_TO from TSMC for second-order (ASML) exposure
Attach the grounding span for every edge on the path

tsmc_exposure.cypher:
MATCH (f:Fund)-[h:HOLDS]->(c:Company)-[s:SUPPLIES_TO {criticality:'critical'}]->(t:Company {name:'Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing'})
RETURN f.name AS fund, sum(h.weight_pct) AS exposed_weight, collect(c.name) AS via
ORDER BY exposed_weight DESC

board_interlock.question: Do any board members sit on the boards of two companies we hold?
board_interlock.answer: Yes. Ada Interlock is a director of both NVIDIA (Audit committee) and Microsoft (Compensation committee) — both held by both funds. This is a board interlock across two of the portfolio's largest positions (a combined 20.5% of the Demo Growth Fund and 28.0% of the Demo Focused Growth Fund), which is relevant to independence and governance-concentration review.

citations.title: NVIDIA DEF 14A
citations.span: Ada Interlock has served as a director since 2019 and is a member of the Audit Committee.

plan.strategy: graph pattern match for shared Person across DIRECTOR_OF edges
steps: Keep only companies that are HELD by a Fund
Return the person and the two companies with committee qualifiers

board_interlock.cypher:
MATCH (p:Person)-[:DIRECTOR_OF]->(c:Company)<-[:HOLDS]-(:Fund)
WITH p, collect(DISTINCT c.name) AS boards
WHERE size(boards) >= 2
RETURN p.name AS person, boards

disclosure_gap.question: Is the funds' supply-chain / foundry risk disclosed in their prospectus?
disclosure_gap.answer: No — this is a disclosure coverage gap. NVIDIA, AMD, Apple, Broadcom and TSMC are all EXPOSED_TO the 'Advanced foundry / supply concentration' risk factor (category supply_chain), and both funds hold those issuers, but neither fund's 485BPOS prospectus has a principal-risk section that COVERS that risk factor. The prospectuses cover technology, customer/sector concentration and regulatory risk, but not the foundry-concentration exposure that the holdings actually carry.

citations.title: NVIDIA FY2025 10-K
citations.span: We depend on a limited number of foundries, principally Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), for the fabrication of our GPUs

graph_paths.label: … but no COVERS edge from either prospectus

plan.strategy: anti-join: exposure edges present, matching COVERS edges absent
steps: Find RiskFactor nodes with an inbound EXPOSED_TO from a held Company
Left-join DisclosureSection-[:COVERS]->RiskFactor for the funds' forms
Return risk factors where the COVERS side is null (the gap)

disclosure_gap.cypher:
MATCH (c:Company)<-[:HOLDS]-(:Fund)
MATCH (c)-[:EXPOSED_TO]->(rf:RiskFactor {category:'supply_chain'})
WHERE NOT EXISTS { MATCH (:DisclosureSection)-[:COVERS]->(rf) }
RETURN DISTINCT rf.title AS uncovered_risk, collect(DISTINCT c.name) AS exposed_issuers

customer_concentration.question: What is driving NVIDIA's customer-concentration risk right now?
customer_concentration.answer: NVIDIA discloses that a limited number of hyperscale customers account for a substantial portion of its data-center revenue; in the graph, Microsoft, Meta and Amazon are all modelled as CUSTOMER_OF NVIDIA and are themselves top-10 holdings in both funds.
